candidates.rationale: First: concrete release office and prospective purchasing sequence; test missing exact remedy, actual staffing/cost and upstream fallback before priority survives.

Second: existing execution programme; becomes preferred on affirmative buyer delegation, quote and consequential workflow if Japan's test fails. Admission and accreditation do not create release authority.

Matched national/common-service comparison: same safeguard may be cheaper through one competent shared host. Require delegation and rights; Belgian scope nests inside the wider envelope and must not be added.

assumptions: A meaningful workflow lies within the documented release office's authority; the incumbent and exact delegation remain unverified.
Prospective contract terms are still changeable; published schedule is a plan, not proof.
Configuration identity, sufficient evidence rights, a non-developing retester and usable fallback can be secured.
Reversibility, service continuity and fair supplier access are explicit values; they cannot excuse negligible consequential coverage.

objections.claim: Platform vulnerability controls and procurement awards do not establish a signed supplier-bound model-safety remedy. Downstream suppliers may lack upstream evidence or retirement control.

A tractable drafting pilot may cover too little serious activity. Require an actual sensitive-data/tool-action inventory and transaction denominator; reconsider rights-enforcement evidence if only demonstration tasks qualify.
Fixed external certification or blanket upstream disclosure can favour incumbents. The packet records mechanisms and stakeholder objections, not population-wide exclusion rates.

unknowns: Incumbent decision-maker, exact delegation, tender amendability, signed acceptance/cure terms and actual exercise of the proposed model-safety hold.
Named available staff, loaded rates, review queue, cloud/inference charges, supplier preparation burden, recurring retest cost and funded envelope.
Eligible smaller supplier participation and reasons for withdrawal; substantive evidence access and confidential handling rights.
Normal gated transaction volume, consequential actions, manual fallback quality, substitution/bypass and actual harm outcomes.
LUMI annex delegation and evaluator permissions; Singapore purchaser identity, quote and admission authority; cross-border evidence acceptance.

validationTest.name: Two-supplier, one-workflow version-change acceptance rehearsal
validationTest.status: Proposal only; no contact, consent or execution claimed
preconditions: Actual approver and contracting officer; delegation and changeable lawful instrument
One consequential workflow; larger and smaller capable supplier paths within procurement eligibility
Named-person availability and itemised quote; buyer-funded maximum cost and staff-days fixed before results
Approved synthetic-data staging, disabled external actions, scoped evidence access and non-developing retester
validationTest.staffCost: Record purchaser/contract review, workflow owner, integration, independent retest, privacy and fallback functions; functions are not assumed hires. Measure hours times loaded rates plus cloud and supplier costs, queue time and recurring update burden against ordinary acceptance. No defensible numeric budget or available staffing is in the packet.
validationTest.method: Randomised clean tasks, held-out leakage/action failures and seeded material version change or retirement in a staging copy exercising the actual release pipeline permission boundary. Record failed approval, technical hold, useful previous/manual fallback, correction and fresh independently scored retest.

proposedThresholds.criticalFailures: Any seeded critical disclosure or unauthorised action blocks that build; no release while unresolved
proposedThresholds.utility: At least90% of baseline successful clean-task completion and no loss of essential service; owner must validate suitability before execution
proposedThresholds.resources: Within predeclared funded cost and available staff-day caps; both supplier paths can meet the same outcome standard

metrics: Detected/missed critical defects and fresh retest results
False holds, task completion, fallback delay and failures
Actual staff-days, loaded cost, queue and repeat-change cost
Supplier evidence gaps, preparation burden, withdrawals and eligibility constraints
Joined workflow/version/permission inventory, normal transaction denominator and excluded/bypassed activity
falsifiers: Quote cannot be funded or staff cannot be assigned
Seeded failing version escapes hold or fresh retest fails
Fallback destroys essential service or utility misses the predeclared floor
Unnecessary fixed evidence burdens exclude a comparable capable smaller supplier
Only negligible-consequence demonstration activity is governable
validationTest.reversal: On failure, prefer the equivalent Singapore purchaser test only with affirmative delegation, quote and consequential workflow. LUMI requires affirmative delegation/workload/cost evidence. Otherwise record no validated ready route.
validationTest.scopeLimit: A staging pass is not measured real-world harm reduction, whole-model safety, international consent or proof of production coverage.

ideas.name: Proportionate acceptance pack and cost ledger
ideas.design: Buyer-funded reusable baseline harness where lawful; equivalent scoped evidence and separately priced application retests; necessary confidential examination without blanket training-data escrow. Record conflicts, supplier effort and abandoned bids; test savings and unchanged critical outcomes.

ideas.name: Common receipt, local decision
ideas.design: Only after a working local hold, reuse matching version/tool/permission fields in the LUMI national/common pair or willing purchasers; retain local rights/acceptance decisions, measure duplicate hours and additional governed work, withdraw portability on unexplained disagreement.

dissent: Dissent I would defend: a certificate, procurement completion or staging demonstration is not a delivered safeguard. Demand an exercised authorised restriction, correction, fresh retest and useful service at known cost. Do not require inaccessible upstream information from small suppliers while rewarding incumbent paperwork; do not perpetuate low-impact pilots when an evidenced harmful operation offers the more consequential test.
